prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas. Injury: knee injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1332; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not state my full name on the record right now. Can you just use "the plaintiff"?

Q: We can note that you've declined for now, but I'll need your full name before we finish. Let's start with the accident. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving through an intersection in Conroe, Texas. I had a green light, or at least I believed I did.

Q: Which direction were you traveling?

A: I was heading straight through the intersection on the main road.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle came from my right side and went through the intersection. It struck the driver's side of my car. The impact pushed my car sideways and I hit the door and the center console.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?

A: No, I was conscious the entire time. I was dazed, and my knee was hurting almost right away.

Q: Did you see the other driver's signal before the collision?

A: I did not notice a signal. I was looking ahead and I didn't see them until they were already in the intersection.

Q: Which part of your body was injured?

A: My left knee. It struck the dashboard and the console. It swelled up within a few hours and I couldn't put weight on it that evening.

Q: Where did you receive treatment first?

A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and gave me a brace and crutches. Then I was referred to an orthopedic doctor.

Q: Have you continued treatment since then?

A: Yes. I've had physical therapy several times a week, and the doctor has discussed whether I'll need further procedures.

Q: How has the knee affected your daily life?

A: I used to walk my dog every morning and play in a recreational softball league. I've stopped both. Stairs are difficult, and I need help carrying groceries. I also had to take time off from my job, which I do in a warehouse, because standing for long shifts causes significant pain.

Q: Have you had any prior problems with that knee?

A: No. Before this accident I had no ongoing issues with it.

Q: Thank you. We'll take a short break now, and I'll need your full name when we resume.
